memory_candidates.content: When validating a candidate fix that is empirically motivated rather than principled (e.g. a Z3 alpha-rename perturbing MBQI/E-matching heuristics), a 3-5-probe sample at the solver's DEFAULT (unpinned) random-seed parameters is not evidence about the candidate's general reliability -- it is evidence about that one specific default draw. A real >= 20-seed PINNED sweep can reverse the conclusion entirely: in this case the renamed construction looked strictly better on 3 default-parameter probes (3/3 fast decided vs. 3/3 timeout) but was actually WORSE than the unmodified construction under a 25-pinned-seed sweep (5/25 undecided vs. 2/25). Always run the real seed-sweep gate BEFORE trusting a small default-parameter sample, and run it against a same-host, same-budget baseline control at the same seeds, not just the candidate alone -- otherwise a favorable single point in the seed space is mistaken for a fix.
